request.content: You are a helpful assistant that translates programming worked examples into other natural languages, maintaining both technical accuracy and the original code formatting.

[[TASK-DEFINITION]] You will be given a worked example. Your job is to translate the [[WORKED-EXAMPLE]] according to the [[TASK-INSTRUCTIONS]]. [[WORKED-EXAMPLE]] [[PROGRAM-NAME]] Determining the Average Rating for Each Soda in The Survey [[PROGRAM-DESCRIPTION]] Suppose a soda manufacturer held a taste test for four new flavors to determine if people liked them. The manufacturer got 10 people to try each new flavor and give it a score from 1 to 5, where 1 equals poor and 5 equals excellent. The results of that survey is stored in a matrix. Each row of the matrix holds the responses that all testers gave for one particular soda flavor, and each column holds the responses of one person for all sodas.\nConstruct a program that determines the average ratings that respondents provided to four new flavors of soda. [[SOURCE-CODE]] [[LINE01]] #Step 1: Define a 4x10 two-dimensional list [[LINE02]] ratings_data = [[3, 4, 5, 2, 1, 4, 3, 2, 4, 4], [[LINE03]] [2, 4, 3, 4, 3, 3, 2, 1, 2, 2], [[LINE04]] [3, 5, 4, 5, 5, 3, 2, 5, 5, 5], [[LINE05]] [1, 1, 1, 3, 1, 2, 1, 3, 2, 4]] [[LINE06]] #Step 2: Get the dimensions of the list that stores the ratings data [[LINE07]] num_sodas = len(ratings_data) [[LINE08]] num_respondents = len(ratings_data[0]) [[LINE09]] #Step 3: Create a list to store the sum of rating of each soda flavor [[LINE10]] soda_sum = [0] * num_sodas [[LINE11]] #Step 4: Iterate through the sodas [[LINE12]] for i in range(num_sodas): [[LINE13]] #Step 4.1: Calculate the sum of the ratings for the soda i+1 [[LINE14]] for j in range(num_respondents): [[LINE15]] soda_sum[i] += ratings_data[i][j] [[LINE16]] #Step 5: Calculate and print the average rating for each soda [[LINE17]] print("Averages:") [[LINE18]] for i in range(num_sodas): [[LINE19]] print("Soda # {:d} : {:.2f}".format((i+1), soda_sum[i]/num_respondents)) [[LINE-EXPLANATIONS]] [[LINE02.EXPL1]] We need to use two-dimensional list (a list of lists) to create a matrix of the ratings. This statement creates a 4x10 two-dimensional list called ratings_data of ratings given to 4 new flavors of soda by 10 respondents. [[LINE02.EXPL2]] Note that each matrix row corresponds to a sublist in the two-dimensional list. Also, note that lists can naturally span multiple lines if we want them to because they are contained by a pair of brackets. [[LINE07.EXPL1]] We store the number of rows in the ratings_data in variable num_sodas because we'll use it in different steps of the program. Note that the function len(ratings_data) returns the number of rows in the ratings_data [[LINE08.EXPL1]] We store the number of columns in the ratings_data in variable num_respondents because we'll use it in different steps of the program. Note that the function len(ratings_data[0]) returns the number of columns in the ratings_data [[LINE10.EXPL1]] To calculate the average ratings for sodas, we need to first calculate the sum of the ratings for the four new flavors of sodas and then divide the sum of the ratings given to each soda by the total number of respondents. We need four variables to find the sum of the ratings that each of the four new flavors of soda received, which means that a list is a great way to store this data. In general, whenever we find ourselves thinking that we need n of some kind of data, we should think about using a list of length n. Here, we need four variables for storing the maximum rating for each soda; so, we create a list of length 4. [[LINE10.EXPL2]] The first, second, third, and fourth element in the list will be used for storing the sum of the ratings that the first, second, third, and fourth soda received. In this statement, we create the list and fill it with 0s. The zeros will be later replaced by the ratings from respondents. [[LINE10.EXPL3]] We use the repetition operator * to create the list soda_max. The repetition operator makes N copies of this list and joins them all together into a single list, where N is the number of sodas stored in variable num_sodas, here, 4. Note that when the operand on the left side of the * is a list, it becomes the repetition operator and not the multiplication. [[LINE12.EXPL1]] We need to process the rating data and calculate the sum of the ratings for each soda (row totals). Our data, that is stored in ratings_data, is a two-dimensional list; therefore, we need to use nested for loops to process all of its elements. This statement is the outer for loop in the nested loop and it processes the data stored in ratings_data row by row. [[LINE12.EXPL2]] To iterate over the rows in the ratings_data, we need the indexes to start at 0 with every integer number up to but not including the number of rows. We get this sequence by calling the range(num_sodas) function. Note that variable num_sodas stores the number of rows in the ratings_data. [[LINE14.EXPL1]] This statement is the inner loop of the nested loop. It processes the elements within the row i where i is the row index in the ratings_data that changes after each iteration of the outer loop. To iterate over the individual elements in each row (i.e., iterating over the columns within a row) in the ratings_data, we need the indexes to start at 0 with every integer number up to but not including the number of columns. We get this sequence by calling the range(num_respondents) function. [[LINE14.EXPL2]] Note that variable num_respondents stores the number of columns in the ratings_data. Also, note that the name that we choose for the index in the inner loop should be different from the index name in the outer for loop. Here, we choose i for the row index and j for the column index. [[LINE15.EXPL1]] This statement adds the value of the current element in row i and column j to the element in the list soda_sum that stores the sum of the ratings for the soda i+1 in the ratings_data. [[LINE15.EXPL2]] More specifically, if i is 0, it adds the current element to the soda_sum[0] that stores the sum of the ratings for the Soda #1; if i is 1, it adds the current element to the soda_sum[1] that stores the sum of the ratings for the Soda #2; and so on. [[LINE15.EXPL3]] Note that the += operator adds the value of the element in row i and column j of the ratings_data (i.e., element ratings_data[i][j]) to the value of the list element soda_sum[i] and the result is stored in the list element soda_sum[i]. Thus, this statement is equivalent to the statement soda_sum[i] = soda_sum[i] + ratings_data[i][j]. [[LINE17.EXPL1]] This statement prints to the default standard output stream the text "Averages:" followed by the end-of-line character at the end. [[LINE18.EXPL1]] We want to calculate and print the average of ratings given to the sodas. To do this, we need to iterate over the sum of the ratings for the sodas stored the list soda_sum, we need the indexes to start at 0 with every integer number up to but not including the number of sodas. We get this sequence by calling the range(num_sodas) function. Remember the number of sodas is stored in variable num_sodas. [[LINE19.EXPL1]] We get the average rating for a soda by dividing the sum of the ratings given to that soda by the number of respondents stored in variable num_respondents. We call the format function to format how this floating-point number should be printed.
We use {:d} to print the decimal argument of the format function (i.e., the soda number which we get by calling i+1), and {:.2f} to print the floating-point argument of the format function (average of ratings for soda i+1) with just two decimal digits. [[LINE19.EXPL2]] Notice that the format specification inside a pair of curly braces starts with a : and followed by the text that specifies how the value should be presented by stating its data type. The data type d requires a decimal argument while the data type f requires a floating-point argument. An error will occur if the argument is not the expected data type. Note that the / operator performs the real division, producing a floating point result; thus, the average is a floating-point number [[LINE19.EXPL3]] The format function returns the result of replacing each {…} placeholder in the template string with its corresponding argument passed to the format function. Anything else, which is not contained in curly braces will be literally printed, i.e. without any changes. [[LINE19.EXPL4]] The printed text is followed by the end-of-line character at the end. [[LINE-DISTRACTORS]] [[DIST1.LC]] soda_sum = [0] * num_respondents [[DIST2.LC]] for i in range(num_respondents): [[DIST3.LC]] for j in range(num_sodas): [[DIST4.LC]] soda_sum[i] = ratings_data[i][j] [[DIST5.LC]] soda_sum[j] = ratings_data[i][j] [[TASK-INSTRUCTIONS]] Translate the given worked example into Arabic. Be sure to specifically translate the sections labeled [[PROGRAM-NAME]], [[PROGRAM-DESCRIPTION]], [[SOURCE-CODE]], [[LINE-EXPLANATIONS]], and [[LINE-DISTRACTORS]]. In the [[SOURCE-CODE]] section, translate ONLY user-defined string-literals and comments; make sure they are ASCII-folded (i.e., remove any accents or non-ASCII characters). Preserve the original format and Do NOT add, remove, or change any content beyond translation.

[[LINE19.EXPL3]] تعيد دالة format نتيجة استبدال كل موضع {…} في سلسلة القالب بالوسيط المقابل الممرَّر إلى الدالة. أي شيء آخر غير محتوى الأقواس المعقوفة سيُطبع حرفيًا، أي بدون تغييرات. [[LINE19.EXPL4]] النص المطبوع يتبعه فاصل سطر في النهاية.
